# One claim, opened once, held across a subgraph

An acquirer node opens a claim; downstream nodes co-hold the same claim through
the `holds` directive. The producer sees one Open for the whole holding
subgraph, and exactly one terminal verb at the end of it: Commit when every
holder succeeds, Abandon when any holder fails.

## The deployment

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db

claim_producers:
  "stage-store":
    endpoint: "grpc://stage-store:9441"
    write_semantics_allowed: ["sync"]

named_locks: {}
executors: {}
```

## The template

```yaml
name: claim-handoff-commit
version: v1
nodes:
  - type: acquirer
    executor: http-node
    claim_producers:
      - name: stage-store
        selector: "/stage/{{params.run}}"
        intent: rw
        alias: staged
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:    {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19439/rec/acquirer"}
          method: {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr:   {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.address}}"}
          held_scope:  {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.claim_scope}}"}
          held_region: {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.payload.region}}"}

  - type: writer
    executor: http-node
    holds:
      staged: {from: acquirer}
    subscribes:
      - node: acquirer
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    error_types:
      "http/server_error/500": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:    {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19439/rec/writer"}
          method: {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr:   {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.address}}"}
          held_scope:  {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.claim_scope}}"}
          held_region: {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.payload.region}}"}

  - type: verifier
    executor: http-node
    holds:
      staged: {from: acquirer}
    subscribes:
      - node: writer
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    error_types:
      "http/server_error/500": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:    {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19439/rec/verifier"}
          method: {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr:   {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.address}}"}
          held_scope:  {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.claim_scope}}"}
          held_region: {type: string, source: "{{claim.staged.payload.region}}"}
```

`holds: {staged: {from: acquirer}}` is the whole declaration. Each co-holder
reads the live claim by alias — its address, a payload field, and the scope
bytes — straight into its own attribute schema.

## Drive it

```bash
rimsky template deploy "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky instance create "$TPL" --params '{"run":"good"}' --endpoint "$BASE" -o json

curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: wake-$IID" \
  -d '{"type":""}'

rimsky instance nodes "$IID" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/claim-handles?limit=200"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/claim-handles/$CLAIM_HANDLE_ID/holders"
```

## When every holder succeeds

The acquirer, the writer and the verifier each settle fresh.

The producer receives exactly one `Open` for the whole holding subgraph and
exactly one `Commit`, with no `Abandon`. The claim is taken once for the shape,
not once per node.

Each co-holder receives the acquirer's own values:

```json
{"held_addr": "stage-store://stage/good",
 "held_region": "eu-west-1",
 "held_scope": "{\"selector\":\"/stage/good\"}"}
```

The co-holders' address is byte-identical to the acquirer's, so no node
re-acquired anything to do its work against the staged location.

The claim handle ends `committed`, and the holders route reports three holders
on that one claim.

## When any holder fails

Run the same template with the verifier's endpoint answering 500.

The producer still receives exactly one `Open` for the selector — and then
`Abandon`, with no `Commit`. All three nodes settle failed with
`terminal/error/abandoned`, and the claim handle ends `abandoned`.

That is the all-or-nothing half: a stage-then-write-then-verify pipeline built
this way cannot leave a partially written claim committed because one member of
the subgraph did not succeed.
